messages:
monitor-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple pods on gpu-node-12 reporting repeated CUDA illegal memory access errors (OOMs + container restarts). Error rate spiking for /v1/generate and /v1/embed routes. See alert: https://prometheus.local/alerts/INC-5337774444

jordan: seeing this in the dashboard too. node gpu-node-12 has 6 pods crashlooping, kernel logs contain 'invalid device address' and pagewalk faults. tagging @sre-night and @kerneldriver-team

maya: oncall I'm here — grabbing logs. any customer-visible 5xxs yet?

alex: yes, embed pipeline showing ~12% 5xx for last 2m. CS reported one customer (Acme) with errors in their production run.

oncall-bot: @sre-night is now oncall for incidents (handing off). Please update status channel when you have comms.

jordan: quick triage: OOMs correlate with kernel pagewalks in dmesg: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679010] BUG: kernel NULL pointer dereference in __do_page_fault+0x...
[ 12345.679015] CUDA: illegal memory access at address 0xdeadbeef
```

maya: interesting — also seeing repeated `driver:misaligned-pte` traces in the device driver logs. could be a kernel SMMU/IOVA mapping race.

alex: steps I'm taking: cordon + drain planning for gpu-node-12, spin up replacement node. planning graceful drain: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

jordan: hold drain for 30s — we want a memory dump and NV syslog from the node for kernel team. @kerneldriver-team can you pick this up?

kerneldriver-team: grabbing dmesg and core dumps now. please keep node alive if possible, we'll collect a kdump. what's kernel version on that node?

maya: kernel 5.15.0-88, nvidia driver 530.11, container runtime runc 1.0.4. models running are llm-large-int8.

customer-success: flagged Acme (acct 4721) and added incident tag. told them we're investigating and will update in 15m.

oncall-bot: created internal incident INC-5337774444; created status page incident PROD-5337774444.

jordan: collected kdump and /var/log/messages tarball, uploading to S3: `s3://redwood-debug/INC-5337774444/gpu-node-12/`

kerneldriver-team: download link received. early signal: looks like a race in the pagewalk path when eviction and GPU DMA overlap — reproducer needed but dump shows corrupted PTE for device mapping.

maya: probable mitigation options?

alex: immediate mitigation: 1) cordon & drain to stop new pods landing on node; 2) shift traffic from model route to fallback quantized model on different pool; 3) restart node after dump.

jordan: agreed. executing drain now, moving canary traffic. `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12` -> done. starting drain (evicting pods that can be rescheduled).

maya: I'm updating routing: switching /v1/embed to quantized-embeddings-v1 on dedicated pool to reduce GPU pressure. fallback config in console -> rollout set to 100% quantized.

alex: customer-impact note: some in-progress requests will get 5xx; new requests should start hitting fallback within ~45s. CS please update Acme with ETA ~10m for stabilization.

customer-success: will update Acme and post to status page: "We are seeing degraded performance and errors for embedding and generate endpoints affecting a subset of customers; mitigation in progress. Next update in 10 minutes."

kerneldriver-team: reproduction/mitigation plan: try to reproduce under kernel 5.15+nv530; if repro, patch driver to add tighter serialization around IOVA updates. If not, consider disabling concurrent eviction path as hotfix.

jordan: after drain completes, we're going to reboot node to clear GPU state and re-run suite. if errors persist on replacement node, escalate to rollback drivers or isolate fleet.

oncall-bot: handoff note: @sre-night will lead next 30m, @kerneldriver-team owns triage/root-cause. Post updates here and in incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/INC-5337774444

maya: drain finished, node empty. rebooting now. `ssh root@gpu-node-12 sudo reboot`

alex: replacement node joined cluster, starting reschedules. monitoring for new CUDA errors.

jordan: quick probe logs from replacement show one early OOM but not deviceaddr faults. keep watching.

kerneldriver-team: we've started a stress repro on identical kernel/driver config; feeding continuous eviction + allocation. will report if we can reproduce.

customer-success: posted status update to customers.

maya: if repro is confirmed, plan will be: 1) open CVE-style internal advisory for driver rollback, 2) push hotfix to Dedicated pool to force fallback to older driver version, 3) staged rollout.

jordan: for now incident severity set to Sev2, customer impact medium. tagging oncall for longer-term follow-up.

oncall-bot: reminder: collect any core dumps and attach to incident before closing.

alex: monitoring shows error rate back to baseline after switch to quantized pool. will keep watch for next 30m.

kerneldriver-team: repro test created a soft-failure after ~12min; dump captured. sharing preliminary notes in the incident doc.

jordan: thanks all. next update in 20m or on-change. :thumbsup:
